weak_reason: R-squared = 8.8% against the 10% weak-instrument threshold; the 90% confidence interval [0.17, 0.37] spans 0.72x the point estimate

adopted.basis: tier-1 own-stock weekly regression (usability gate PASSED)
adopted.why: n = 216 weekly observations, R-squared = 0.088 against the 0.05 floor, SE(beta) = 0.060 against |beta| = 0.271. All three conditions of the usability gate are met, so the regression estimate is adopted rather than a default.
adopted.corroboration: Cross-checked two ways. (i) The Dimson sum-beta is 0.194 with a 90% interval of [0.00, 0.39]; the adopted 0.27 sits inside it. (ii) The simple prior for a cyclical, capital-intensive materials business is 1.0-1.5 and for a defensive or staple business 0.6-0.9; the adopted figure is read against both in the study rather than accepted at face value.

dimson.note: Dimson (1979) sum-beta over one lead, the contemporaneous term and two lags. The uplift over the contemporaneous OLS beta measures how much co-movement is booked late because the stock does not trade on every session.

self_inclusion_bias.note: Leaving the subject inside its own equal-weight index injects a self-covariance term into the numerator. The excluding figure is the correct one and is what is reported; the including figure is disclosed so the size of the contamination is visible rather than assumed away.

thin_trading.note: Share of sessions closing unchanged, against the median of the Egyptian library. A high ratio is the documented mechanism for a downward-biased contemporaneous beta.

plausibility.net_cash_note: The company carries roughly 0.8x net debt to EBITDA and its earnings are levered to a global commodity price benchmark, both of which argue for an estimate at or above the cyclical band rather than below it.
